page: Hetzner Cloud cpx21 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 3 shared vCPUs with 3 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.3 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng, while multi-core CPU performance is average. Memory bandwidth is a bottleneck, with read-only large block speeds and write speeds ranking in the bottom 25 percent, and the PassMark memory score ranking in the bottom 10 percent. Cryptographic capabilities are average, with PassMark CPU encryption scoring 3332.13. For lightweight machine learning, LLM inference using a small 135M model achieves average speeds of 453.69 tokens per second for prompt processing and 158.27 tokens per second for text generation.

The cpx21 offers a budget-friendly hardware profile with local NVMe storage, but users face clear performance tradeoffs. The shared CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio limit its capability under sustained multi-threaded workloads, as evidenced by weak multi-core Geekbench and software compilation scores. However, for workloads requiring high single-core burst capacity without high memory demands, the resource density is highly cost-efficient.

This server is suited for lightweight, non-memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, small-scale text processing, lightweight single-threaded tasks, and development or testing environments that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high memory bandwidth.

This resource profile presents a cost-efficient option for budget-conscious deployments where high memory capacity is not required. The cpx21 is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, text processing, and development environments that benefit from strong single-threaded performance but do not demand sustained multi-core execution or high memory throughput.
